_comment: Production-dependency advisories (npm audit --omit=dev) that are known and deliberately not failing the scan YET. Read by scripts/security/static-scan.mjs and the CI 'dependencies' job. Rules: every entry needs a truthful reason, an owner and an expiry at most 90 days away (these were set 30 to 60 days out on 2026-11-11); an expired entry stops protecting anything and the scan fails again. status 'needs-fix' means the finding is real and reachable, the entry only defers the failure. status 'mitigated' / 'not-applicable' / 'accepted-risk' say why it is not exploitable today. Review each entry when it expires; do not just move the date.

entries.reason: FIXED by upgrading Next 14.2.35 -> 15.5.29 on 2026-11-11 (the fix is in 15.5.x). This entry only remains until it expires because the baseline test pins it. Original finding: REAL. The web app is an App Router app (client/src/app), and nginx forwards / to Next, so React Server Components request handling is reachable by anyone who can reach the web port: unauthenticated denial of service of the web tier (the API is a separate process and is not affected). Not exploitable for data theft. Fix: upgrade next 14.2.x to 15.5.x or 16 (GATE item 1 in docs/SECURITY_AUDIT.md), planned as its own change with a staging soak. Interim: nginx request timeouts, container restart policy.

FIXED by upgrading Next 14.2.35 -> 15.5.29 on 2026-11-11 (the fix is in 15.5.x). This entry only remains until it expires because the baseline test pins it. Original finding: REAL. Denial of service with Server Components, reachable by an anonymous visitor on any App Router deployment (see GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf). Web tier only. Fixed only by the Next major upgrade (15.5.x / 16).

FIXED by upgrading Next 14.2.35 -> 15.5.29 on 2026-11-11 (the fix is in 15.5.x). This entry only remains until it expires because the baseline test pins it. Original finding: REAL. Second denial of service with Server Components (see GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf); reachable anonymously, web tier only. Fixed only by the Next major upgrade (15.5.x / 16).

FIXED by upgrading Next 14.2.35 -> 15.5.29 on 2026-11-11 (the fix is in 15.5.x). This entry only remains until it expires because the baseline test pins it. Original finding: LIKELY REAL. SSRF through WebSocket upgrade requests handled by Next. The nginx proxy profile forwards Upgrade headers for the / location to the web container, so the upgrade path is reachable from outside. Not exploited here; phase G of docs/SECURITY_AUDIT_PLAN.md tests it against the test stack. Fix: Next major upgrade; interim: stop forwarding Upgrade on / (only /socket.io needs it) once dev hot reload is not needed in the container.

Remote code execution through the Image Optimization API (SVG). The optimizer is disabled: client/next.config.js sets images.unoptimized: true and has no remotePatterns, client/src/__tests__/next-config-headers.test.ts pins both, and /_next/image answers 404 (checked on the local web server 2026-11-11; verify:deploy and the dynamic CI job re-check it against a built stack). It becomes reachable again only if someone removes that setting.

Remote code execution through the Image Optimization API (AVIF). Same mitigation as GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw: images.unoptimized is true, no remotePatterns, /_next/image answers 404, a unit test pins the configuration.

Remote code execution that only affects Next servers running on Windows. Production runs the web app in node:20-alpine (client/Dockerfile); the Windows development machine runs next dev on localhost only. Never host the web app on Windows until Next is upgraded.

Middleware bypass in Pages Router applications that use i18n. This app uses only the App Router and has no i18n configuration in client/next.config.js, so the vulnerable path does not exist. (The login gate also is not the authority: the API checks every request.)

Denial of service in App Router using Server Actions. The code base defines no Server Action (no 'use server' anywhere in client/src). Whether Next still processes the Next-Action header for an unknown action in a way this advisory covers is UNCONFIRMED, so treat it as reachable until the Next upgrade; it shares the fix with the Server Components denial of service entries.

Second denial of service in App Router using Server Actions. No Server Action is defined in client/src; applicability to an app without actions is UNCONFIRMED, so it is treated as reachable until the Next upgrade (same fix as GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf).
SSRF in Server Actions on custom servers. Needs Server Actions (none are defined in client/src) and the web container runs Next's own standalone server.js, not a custom server.

SSRF in rewrites when the destination hostname is attacker-controlled. The only rewrite (client/next.config.js) has a fixed destination origin taken from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL at build time, with no request parameter in the hostname; with the nginx proxy profile the rewrite is not used at all (nginx routes /api straight to the API).

Command injection in the glob command-line tool (-c/--cmd). Nothing runs the glob CLI. The package comes in through eslint-config-next, which client/package.json lists under dependencies instead of devDependencies, so it shows in a production audit although it never ships (the web image copies only Next's standalone output). The real fix is to move eslint, eslint-config-next, typescript and the @types/* packages to devDependencies (npm ci in client/Dockerfile still installs them for the build); that removes this and the minimatch, @typescript-eslint/* and @next/eslint-plugin-next findings from the production tree.

ReDoS in minimatch needs an attacker-chosen glob pattern; here it is only reached by lint tooling (eslint-config-next, @typescript-eslint) with patterns from the repository's own config, at build time. Not in the runtime images. Real fix: move the eslint packages to devDependencies (see the glob entry).

ReDoS in minimatch matchOne with repeated globstar segments: needs an attacker-chosen pattern; only lint tooling at build time uses it, with the repository's own patterns. Not in the runtime images. Real fix: move the eslint packages to devDependencies (see the glob entry).

ReDoS in minimatch with nested extglobs: needs an attacker-chosen pattern; only lint tooling at build time uses it, with the repository's own patterns. Not in the runtime images. Real fix: move the eslint packages to devDependencies (see the glob entry).

Arbitrary file read through an attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL comment in CSS. The vulnerable copy is the postcss nested inside next, used at build time on this repository's own CSS and Tailwind output; no user-supplied CSS is ever processed at runtime. Goes away with the Next upgrade.

Path traversal when postcss auto-loads a previous source map named in a CSS comment. Same situation as GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q: build time, own CSS only, nothing user-supplied reaches it. Goes away with the Next upgrade.

Mitigated 2026-11-11 (R3-01). The advisory names zod 4's array code; this repo uses the zod 3 API, which has the same class: one issue per failing element. Every list in a request body is now bounded BEFORE its elements are checked (boundedList in server/src/utils/validators.ts, test server/src/__tests__/utils/boundedLists.test.ts: a 200,000-element body yields at most 5 issues) and the validate middleware returns at most 20 truncated details. The zod 4 upgrade is optional.
